title: Composite Index Design
description: Design multi-column indexes that match query predicates and sort orders

data.text: Composite indexes cover queries with multiple predicates or sorts. Column order matters: the index supports leftmost prefixes, so putting high-selectivity columns first is critical.

data.title: Key principles
items: Index on (a, b, c) supports queries on a
Also supports (a, b) and (a, b, c)
Does not support (b, c) or (c) alone
Order columns by selectivity and query frequency

data.title: Composite index for orders
data.content: Queries filter by customer_id and status, then sort by created_at.
data.code:
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer_status_date
ON orders(customer_id, status, created_at DESC);

-- Supported queries:
-- WHERE customer_id = 123
-- WHERE customer_id = 123 AND status = 'shipped'
-- WHERE customer_id = 123 AND status = 'shipped'
--   ORDER BY created_at DESC

data.title: Warning
data.text: Adding too many composite indexes increases write cost. Focus on the most frequent and selective query patterns.

items.question: Should I create separate single-column indexes instead?
items.answer: No. The database usually cannot combine them efficiently for multi-column filters.

items.question: Does index order affect performance?
items.answer: Yes. Higher-selectivity columns first reduces the index scan range.

items.question: Can I include non-filtered columns?
items.answer: Use INCLUDE columns for covering indexes rather than adding them to the key.

data.title: Summary
points: Use leftmost prefix to match query predicates
Include sort columns for ordered results
data.takeaway: Composite index design is about matching the exact query shape, not just filtering columns.
